children: Alstom said it signed an agreement with rolling-stock leasing company Northrail for the delivery of shunting locomotives with a potential value of up to 700 million euros ($801.5 million).

The French train maker on Wednesday said the order for its new Traxx Shunter platform paved the way for the commercial launch of a new generation of shunting locomotives. It added that the order would be booked in the second quarter of its fiscal 2027 year.
A shunting locomotive--also known as a switcher or yard switcher--is a type of locomotive designed for moving railway cars over short distances.

The company said the deal, which amounts to just under 100 million euros for deployment in Germany, covers the supply of up to 100 Traxx Shunter locomotives, with first deliveries scheduled for late 2029.

Alstom said the framework with Northrail-- one of Europe's leading rolling-stock leasing companies--also encompasses 10 years of maintenance services. It also has options for additional locomotives, including for deployment in France, and up to 20 years of maintenance.
